stem: (Select TWO.) A reviewer at Ironclad Insurance runs `terraform plan -out=tfplan` against a configuration where an instance's AMI attribute changed in a way that forces the instance to be recreated. Which two statements are accurate?

choices.text: The plan reports the instance as a single "replace" action rather than as two separate destroy and add lines
Saving the plan with -out changes which actions are proposed for the instance
A forced-recreate change is always reported as two unrelated lines, one destroy and one add
The saved tfplan file can later be used to carry out exactly the actions shown, without recomputing them
The tfplan file can be edited by hand before it is used, to change which resources it affects

rationale: A change that forces recreation is shown as a single replace action, and a plan saved with -out is a file that can later be carried out exactly as reviewed, without being recomputed. Saving a plan to a file does not change what actions were computed; -out only writes the already-computed plan somewhere. A forced-recreate change is not reported as two unrelated lines; replace ties them together as one action. The saved plan file is an opaque format, not something meant to be hand-edited beforehand.
